```{r}
#| include: false
# library(): loads a package so its functions can be used in this session.
# normalizePath(): resolves a path into a canonical absolute path.
# getwd(): returns the current working-directory path.
# file.exists(): checks whether each specified file path exists.
# file.path(): joins path components with the platform-appropriate separator.
# dirname(): returns the directory portion of a file path.
# read.csv(): reads a comma-separated file into a data frame; its first row supplies column names by default.
# factor(): stores categorical values; levels fixes their permitted order and labels can rename their display.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
project <- normalizePath(getwd())
while (!file.exists(file.path(project,"20261.Rproj")) && dirname(project)!=project) project <- dirname(project)
restaurants <- read.csv(file.path(project,"data/module02/restaurant_ratings.csv"))
restaurants$quality_rating <- factor(restaurants$quality_rating,
 levels=c("Good","Very Good","Excellent"),ordered=TRUE)
```

## Inspection and selection

```{r}
# glimpse(): shows table dimensions, column types, and example values.
# colSums(): sums each column separately.
# is.na(): marks missing values with TRUE; na.rm=TRUE elsewhere removes missing values only when justified.
# anyDuplicated(): returns the position of the first duplicate, or zero if none is found.
# select(): chooses columns by name or selection rule.
# filter(): keeps rows whose logical conditions are TRUE; missing conditions are not retained.
# nrow(): returns the number of rows in a table or matrix.
# arrange(): orders rows by supplied columns; desc() reverses a column to descending order.
# desc(): reverses sorting order to descending inside arrange().
# head(): shows the first n entries or rows, six by default.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# anyNA(): returns TRUE if any value is missing; !anyNA(...) requires no missing values.
glimpse(restaurants)
colSums(is.na(restaurants))
anyDuplicated(restaurants$restaurant_id)
selected <- restaurants |> select(restaurant_id,quality_rating,meal_price_usd) |>
 filter(quality_rating=="Excellent",meal_price_usd>=30)
nrow(selected)
restaurants |> arrange(desc(meal_price_usd),restaurant_id) |> head(5)
stopifnot(nrow(restaurants)==300,!anyNA(restaurants),
 anyDuplicated(restaurants$restaurant_id)==0,nrow(selected)==50)
```

One row represents one restaurant. Fifty Excellent restaurants have prices at least USD 30. Repeated prices may belong to different restaurants, so price alone cannot identify duplicates.

## Derived columns and summaries

```{r}
# mutate(): creates or replaces columns while retaining the original rows.
# cut(): groups numeric values into intervals; breaks sets edges and right=FALSE makes [left,right) intervals.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# anyNA(): returns TRUE if any value is missing; !anyNA(...) requires no missing values.
# count(): counts rows for each combination of supplied categories.
# group_by(): defines groups for subsequent dplyr operations without itself calculating a summary.
# summarise(): reduces each group to summary rows; .groups="drop" removes grouping from the result.
# n(): counts rows in the current dplyr group.
# mean(): computes an average; logical TRUE/FALSE values contribute 1/0, giving a proportion.
# median(): returns the middle sorted value, averaging the middle pair for even sample sizes.
# all(): returns TRUE only when every supplied logical value is TRUE.
# is_grouped_df(): checks whether a tibble still carries dplyr grouping metadata.
prepared <- restaurants |> mutate(price_band=cut(meal_price_usd,c(10,20,30,40,50),right=FALSE),
                                 price_at_least_30=meal_price_usd>=30)
stopifnot(!anyNA(prepared$price_band))
restaurants |> count(quality_rating)
summary <- restaurants |> group_by(quality_rating) |>
 summarise(n=n(),mean_price_usd=mean(meal_price_usd),median_price_usd=median(meal_price_usd),.groups="drop")
summary
stopifnot(all(summary$n==c(84,150,66)),all(summary$median_price_usd==c(19.5,25,34.5)),
 !is_grouped_df(summary))
```

## Join and reshape

```{r}
# select(): chooses columns by name or selection rule.
# left_join(): matches tables on the by key while retaining left-table rows; duplicate keys can multiply rows.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# nrow(): returns the number of rows in a table or matrix.
# anyNA(): returns TRUE if any value is missing; !anyNA(...) requires no missing values.
# head(): shows the first n entries or rows, six by default.
# pivot_longer(): turns selected columns into name-value rows using names_to and values_to.
# pivot_wider(): turns name-value rows into columns using names_from and values_from.
lookup <- summary |> select(quality_rating,group_median_usd=median_price_usd)
joined <- restaurants |> left_join(lookup,by="quality_rating")
stopifnot(nrow(joined)==300,!anyNA(joined$group_median_usd))
head(joined)
long <- summary |> select(quality_rating,mean_price_usd,median_price_usd) |>
 pivot_longer(-quality_rating,names_to="measure",values_to="price_usd")
long
long |> pivot_wider(names_from=measure,values_from=price_usd)
```

A lookup with repeated quality keys could multiply matching rows. Check uniqueness before joining and row counts afterward. Missing-value handling must be explicit because exclusions may change group sizes and the population represented by a summary.
